checks.statement: In the NB, rho determines gamma if E is nonempty and E-prime is a G-prime torsor.
checks.reasoning: For a fixed g choose x in E. The equality rho(g.x)=gamma(g).rho(x) determines at most one gamma(g), because the target torsor action is free at rho(x). This holds for every g, so any compatible gamma is unique.
checks.outcome: The uniqueness claim checks out under the written target-torsor and nonempty-source hypotheses. This check did not supply the observed prime marks.

checks.statement: The written vector affine multiplication law (z,gamma).(z-prime,gamma-prime)=(z+gamma(z-prime),gamma gamma-prime).
checks.reasoning: Composing the affine transformations x↦z+gamma(x) and x↦z-prime+gamma-prime(x) gives x↦z+gamma(z-prime)+(gamma gamma-prime)(x), using linearity of gamma.
checks.outcome: The written law agrees with composition in that order. No written sign or variable was corrected from the calculation.
